For warmer afternoons or summer-season scrimmages, the short sleeve training shirt is the right pick. You can order both with the same design so the team can layer up or down per session.

Training shirts are made for hard use, including slide tackles, wall passes, and conditioning drills. Match jerseys come out for game day and stay separate from the practice rotation so they look fresh in team photos and on the broadcast.

faqs.q: Can I layer this under a hoodie or compression top?

The long-sleeve cut intentionally sits looser than a compression top so it layers cleanly without bunching at the shoulder seam.

faqs.q: When should I choose a quarter-zip over a full-zip hoodie, pullover hoodie, or crewneck for soccer
faqs.a: warmups? The quarter-zip goes over the training shirt (or directly over a kit) for the pre-game and dynamic warmup window, where you actually need to vent heat without stopping to take a layer off. On cold training days, layer the quarter-zip on top of the long-sleeve training shirt.

faqs.q: How durable is the zipper and stand collar?
faqs.a: Care: cold wash gentle cycle, zip closed before washing to protect the teeth, inside-out helps the sublimation print, air-dry or low-heat tumble. Avoid high-heat drying because that's what shortens both the zipper slider life and the stand-collar memory.

faqs.q: How does the 4-way stretch handle the full motion range volleyball demands?
faqs.a: Volleyball asks the jersey to do four conflicting things at once: stretch overhead for serves and attacks, compress to the body for passing, breathe through long sets in hot gyms, and stay still on the torso during dives and defensive digs. The ~160 GSM polyester knit with 4-way stretch handles all four. The 4-way stretch means the fabric extends and recovers along BOTH the horizontal and vertical axes — when a player reaches overhead for an attack, the sleeves stretch lengthwise without binding at the shoulder; when they dive forward for a defensive dig, the torso fabric stretches sideways without pulling tight across the chest. Moisture-wicking finish pulls sweat away from the skin and pushes it to the fabric surface where it evaporates, keeping players cool through tournament rounds and back-to-back matches. The full-length sleeve adds the arm coverage without the warmth penalty of cotton — polyester knit is the right fabric for indoor volleyball.

faqs.q: Why does double-knee reinforcement matter on a softball pant?

Double-knee reinforcement adds a second layer of the 220 GSM performance polyester shell across the knee panel , roughly doubling the abrasion resistance exactly where the pant needs it most. It is built into the pant construction, not an add-on, and there is no upcharge for it.

Third, quick changes : at tournaments with tight turnarounds between games, pull-on pants save time. The trade-off is purely about looks: the belted standard pant gives the more traditional, dialed-in varsity look, while the drawstring pant reads slightly more casual. Both are the same 220 GSM performance polyester shell, same double-knee reinforcement, same durability; the choice is whether the program values pull-on convenience or the belted traditional look.

faqs.q: Is the windbreaker a warmth layer, and how water-resistant is it really?
faqs.a: The windbreaker is a wind-and-light-rain shell, not a warmth layer . That is the most important thing to understand before ordering. The water-resistant polyester shell blocks wind and sheds light rain and drizzle, and it has a breathable mesh lining. But it has no fleece insulation, so on a genuinely cold morning it is worn OVER a fleece layer (a crewneck, hoodie, or quarter-zip), not instead of one. On water-resistance specifically: it is water-resistant, not fully waterproof . It will keep a player dry through a passing shower, drizzle, or wind-driven mist, and the shell sheds light rain, but a sustained downpour will eventually soak through, because a truly waterproof seam-sealed rain shell is a different (and much pricier) garment. For softball's typical use (wind on open fields, cool mornings, the occasional light shower), the windbreaker is the right call. If your program plays through heavy rain regularly, layer the windbreaker over a fleece and keep a dry change in the bag.

faqs.q: What counts as a "two-tone" design on the Custom Ice Hockey Two-Tone Jerseys?

The boundary is built into the sublimation file (not stitched on as separate fabric panels). We'll show the boundary placement in the mockup before production starts.

faqs.q: Pullover vs crewneck vs full-zip hoodie — when does the pullover make sense for wrestling?
faqs.a: The pullover hoodie is the choice when the program wants a full uninterrupted front canvas plus head coverage . The crest, school name, and graphics run edge to edge across the chest with no zipper splitting the design, and the attached hood adds warmth for cold gym entries and outdoor travel. Full-zip hoodies trade that uninterrupted canvas for easy on and off (the zipper lets a wrestler peel it at mat side without disturbing headgear or hair). Crewnecks drop the hood entirely for a clean head/neck line that layers under a warmup jacket. Programs often run all three across the roster: the pullover for the bold full-chest team look and team photos, the full-zip for mat-side changes, the crewneck for weigh-in mornings and layering. All three share the same fleece and color-match when ordered together.

faqs.q: Why does the pullover have no zipper — what's the advantage?
faqs.a: Three reasons the pullover skips the zipper. First, the design canvas: with no zipper splitting the front, the crest, school name, and graphics get the full chest surface to run edge to edge, a big clean look for team photos. Second, durability: there is no zipper to snag, jam, or break mid-season. Third, warmth: a full-zip leaves a thin gap and seam down the chest where cold gets in, while the solid pullover front retains warmth through cold-gym practices and recovery sessions. The full-zip is the better pick at mat side. For everything else, the pullover wins on look, durability, and warmth.

faqs.q: Can sublimation hold color on a fleece hoodie — won't it fade on cotton?
faqs.a: It depends on the blend, and this is the question to ask before ordering custom fleece anywhere. Sublimation bonds to polyester fibers , not cotton. On a mostly cotton fleece, the graphics print weak and look washed out. Our pullover hoodies run a performance fleece that takes full sublimation in vibrant color across the full uninterrupted front and stays soft, like a quality varsity piece. faqs.q: How much does an esports jersey cost?
faqs.a: A HAMLO SPORTS esports jersey costs $38.99 per player for 1 to 24, $34.99 for 25 to 50, $32.99 for 51 to 100 and $29.99 for 101 or more. An embroidered crest is optional and priced on your quote.

faqs.q: Can I make my own esports jersey?
faqs.a: Yes. You bring the idea, and a HAMLO SPORTS designer builds it into your jersey: send your logo, a sketch or a reference image with your quote request. Your free mockup comes back within 12 hours, and you can ask for as many changes as you need. Nothing is made until you approve it. If your team doesn't have a logo yet, our designers create one at no extra cost.

faqs.q: Why do esports players wear jerseys?
faqs.a: Esports teams wear jerseys so the roster looks like one team on stream, on stage and in the team photo. The jersey also carries the org's sponsors, and each player's gamertag tells viewers who is who. HAMLO SPORTS sublimates the logos, sponsor marks, gamertags and numbers into every jersey, all included in the price.

faqs.q: How are esports jerseys different from sports jerseys?
faqs.a: An esports jersey is worn for long sessions in a gaming chair and in front of a camera, not for contact or sprinting, so what matters is comfort and how the design reads on screen. HAMLO SPORTS jerseys use lightweight moisture-wicking polyester, and the back usually carries a gamertag, with or without a surname. Sponsor zones sit on the chest, back and sleeves, where viewers see them on stream. The decoration is the same full sublimation we use on our other team jerseys, dyed into the fabric.

faqs.q: What makes a good esports jersey?
faqs.a: A good one stays readable on a phone-sized stream: a gamertag and number big enough to see, sponsor logos where the camera catches them, and team colors that run edge to edge. Sublimation lets HAMLO SPORTS place sponsor marks anywhere on the chest, upper back, shoulders and sleeves, and we lay out your full sponsor list in the free mockup. Comfort counts too, which is why the fabric is lightweight and moisture-wicking.

faqs.q: Can each player have a gamertag instead of a last name?
faqs.a: Yes. Each jersey carries that player's gamertag or name and number, sublimated and included in the price. Send your roster, and every tag appears in your mockup before production.

faqs.q: How long do the jerseys take?
faqs.a: Your jerseys are ready 2 to 3 weeks after you approve the design, then shipping takes 3 to 5 days. The free mockup comes within 12 hours of your request. Put your event date on the quote form so we can plan around it. Need them sooner for a tournament? Ask for free rush on your quote; there's no rush fee, we say yes when production allows, and it's never guaranteed.

faqs.q: Where are HAMLO SPORTS jerseys made?
faqs.a: Designed in the USA, made factory-direct from our Sialkot facility. Our designers build every mockup, and the jerseys ship from our dedicated Sialkot manufacturing facility straight to you.

faqs.q: Which jersey cut should our team choose?
faqs.a: All four cuts take the same sublimated design, and prices differ by cut: short-sleeve and sleeveless from $32.99, long-sleeve from $34.99 and quarter-zip from $38.99 per player (1 to 24). The short sleeve esports jersey is the all-around tournament and stage standard; the long sleeve esports jersey adds full-arm sponsor real estate and warmth in cool LAN venues; the sleeveless esports jersey is the open-shoulder cut for hot stage lighting; and the quarter-zip esports jersey gives an on-demand collar for press, travel, and content days. You can mix cuts across one roster in a single order.
